Highlight Clip: Adam Back: Institutional Allocation Will Drive Bitcoin’s Third Wave of Adoption Adam Back: Institutional Allocation Will Drive Bitcoin’s Third Wave of Adoption On November 1, 2026, Blockstream CEO Adam Back said in an interview with Bitcoin Magazine that Bitcoin's first two waves of adoption were driven by individuals mining and buying Bitcoin, followed by ETFs. The third wave will broaden adoption through professional asset management channels but has yet to fully materialize. Some major investment banks have recommended a 2% to 4% Bitcoin allocation in their model portfolios. More people will gain indirect exposure through mutual funds, pension funds and insurance products, with Bitcoin treasury companies also playing a role. — link

Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Has Remained Below Its ATH for 374 Consecutive Days, Setting an All-Time Record Bitcoin's mining difficulty has spent 374 consecutive days below its all-time high of 155.97 T (set on October 29, 2025), officially marking the longest such stretch in the network's history and surpassing the previous 364-day record from the 2011 crash as well as the 253-day gap following China's 2021 mining ban. The protracted plateau is driven by muted BTC price action (~$76,000) and escalating overhead, prompting publicly listed miners to liquidate Bitcoin reserves and pivot site power toward AI colocation. — link

Coinbase CEO Backs Tokenizing COIN Stock to Broaden the Company's Shareholder Base Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said on X that he supports tokenizing Coinbase stock because he wants more people to own shares in the company. He argued that alienating a potential new category of shareholders is bad for business and that companies should meet customers where they are. Meanwhile, 67 companies, including Apple, Tesla, Nvidia, and Meta, have objected to their own shares being tokenized and traded on OKXICE, a joint venture between OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). These include 56 of the 62 companies initially targeted by the platform, or approximately 90.3%. — link

Singapore's MAS Urges Caution Following Binance Hack, Says Crypto Trading Is Unsuitable for the General Public According to Lianhe Zaobao, a spokesperson for the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said on November 5, in response to the recent Binance hack, that cryptocurrency trading is unsuitable for the general public. Consumers should exercise caution and avoid dealing with unregulated firms. MAS reiterated that Binance is not authorized to provide regulated financial services in Singapore and that, even when trading through licensed firms, regulatory safeguards cannot fully prevent losses arising from the inherent risks of cryptocurrencies. — link
